proposals.before: They treated him as a puppet, letting him have his way in trifles while never truly minding what he did.
proposals.after: Yet Chong and the others treated him like a small child; in a hundred affairs he had a free hand, and at first they did not bother to restrain or keep a record of him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 視之如小兒 and 百事自由 mean they treated Liu Penzi as a child with free rein, not as a puppet limited to trifles; 不恤錄 is failure to supervise or record, not mere indifference.

proposals.before: After Guangwu's death Prince Jing of Shanyang showed so little sorrow at the bier that he was suspected at once; he then sent a secret letter to the Prince of Donghai, goading him into revolt.
proposals.after: After Guangwu's death Prince Jing of Shanyang wept without grief; he composed a flying letter to the Prince of Donghai, urging him to rise in rebellion.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 哭不哀 states only that Jing wept without grief; the idiomatic rendering invents immediate suspicion not present in the source.

proposals.before: In the eighth year of that reign Emperor Huan seized on a solar eclipse as his cue, named the former minister Han Yin metropolitan commandant, and purged the eunuch faction step by step until Luoyang was clean again.
proposals.after: In the eighth year of that reign Emperor Huan seized on a solar eclipse as his cue, named the former Minister of Education Han Yin metropolitan commandant, and purged the eunuch faction step by step until Luoyang was clean again.
proposals.reason: Chinese 故司徒 is the former Minister of Education, not a generic former minister.

proposals.before: He was proved right when the emperor came back from exile and the world slid into chaos.
proposals.after: Later he returned, and thereupon there was great disorder.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 后還，遂大亂 does not name the emperor or mention exile; the idiomatic rendering invents both the subject and the exile.

proposals.before: An edict asked Master of Writing Cai Yong.
proposals.after: An edict asked the gentleman consultant Cai Yong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 議郎 is gentleman consultant, not Master of Writing (尚書).

proposals.before: When Emperor Ai died the empress regent installed Wang Mang's nephew as grand marshal—and chaos followed.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ai died, the empress held the regency; Wang Mang, the empress's elder brother's son, became grand marshal—and chaos followed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 王莽以后兄子爲大司馬 identifies Wang Mang as the empress's elder brother's son appointed grand marshal, not a nephew of Wang Mang.

proposals.before: Xiang Kai argued that the academy had housed the ancient "doubtful" star; when its gate gave way of its own accord, it foretold the collapse of moral culture and the abandonment of education.
proposals.after: Xiang Kai argued that the Imperial Academy was where the former qianyi (palace counselors) had resided; when its gate gave way of its own accord, it foretold the collapse of moral culture and the abandonment of education.
proposals.reason: 前疑 is the office of the former counselors (qianyi), not a 'doubtful' star.

proposals.before: Four years later another parched summer arrived.
proposals.after: In the sixth year, summer, there was drought.
proposals.reason: Yuanchu 6 is the sixth year of that reign title, not four years after Yuanchu 3; the Chinese is 六年夏, matching the literal.

proposals.before: When the boy emperor died, Li Gu the grand commandant begged Liang Ji to choose a mature, virtuous heir so the realm might rally and their own names live on.
proposals.after: When the boy emperor died, Grand Commandant Li Gu urged the empress dowager's brother Liang Ji to establish an heir-emperor, choosing one advanced in years and possessed of virtue, so that if all under Heaven relied on him their merit and fame would not perish.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic omits 太后兄, hiding that Liang Ji is identified as the empress dowager's brother, which the Chinese and literal both state.

proposals.before: Shu was then executed and destroyed.
proposals.after: He was then executed and destroyed.
proposals.reason: The subject 述 is Gongsun Shu's given name, not the region Shu; the idiomatic rendering already names Gongsun Shu.

proposals.before: The long train rolling toward Hejian foretold the emperor's death and the hearse-road that would bring the boy Liu Hong from Hejian to the throne.
proposals.after: The long train rolling toward Hejian foretold the emperor's death and the hearse-road that would bring Emperor Ling from Hejian to the throne.
proposals.reason: Chinese 迎靈帝 names Emperor Ling only; the personal name Liu Hong is not in this unit.

proposals.before: Coins for rooms and gold for halls pictured Lady Dong of Yongle hoarding metal to gild her halls once her son took the throne.
proposals.after: Coins for rooms and gold for halls pictured Empress Dowager Yongle hoarding metal to gild her halls once her son took the throne.
proposals.reason: Chinese 永樂太后 does not give the surname Dong; Lady Dong is an invented identification.

proposals.before: Eunuchs Guan Ba and Su Kang loathed upright scholars; with Liu Ao, Xu Yong, and Liu Fen—they formed a clique; Yuan Shansong's Book notes Liu Fen belonged to the power-broker faction impeached by Fan Pang.
proposals.after: Regular palace attendants Guan Ba and Su Kang loathed outstanding worthies of the realm; with junior privy treasurer of Changle Liu Ao, chamberlain for ceremonies Xu Yong, and secretariat director Liu Fen they formed a clique; Yuan Shansong's Book notes that Liu Fen belonged to the power-broker faction impeached by Fan Pang.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops the offices 長樂少府, 太常, and 尚書 and renders 柳分 as Liu Fen while omitting those titles that identify the men.

proposals.before: In Zhongping 6 the young Liu Xie was hustled to the throne while his brother lacked even a princely rank; dozens of eunuchs led him off with the whole bureaucracy trailing until the party turned back only at the Yellow River.
proposals.after: In Zhongping 6 Marquis Shi mounted the supreme seat; Emperor Xian still had no noble title. He was seized by palace attendant Duan Gui and several tens of others; the dukes, ministers, and all officials followed, and only when they reached the river could they return.
proposals.reason: Chinese distinguishes 史侯, who mounted the throne, from 獻帝, who still had no noble title, and names 段珪; the idiomatic English assigns the accession to Liu Xie.

proposals.before: Since the Guangwu restoration Jingzhou had known peace; under Liu Biao the people prospered—for about eight or nine years.
proposals.after: It means that from the restoration onward Jingzhou had not been broken by disorder, and when Liu Biao became shepherd the people were again abundant and happy; by this point eight or nine years had elapsed.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 中興 rather than the personal name Guangwu.

proposals.before: "Begins to decline" foretold Lady Cai's death and the scattering of Biao's generals.
proposals.after: "When it first declines" means Liu Biao's wife was about to die, and the various generals would fall away and scatter.
proposals.reason: Chinese names only 劉表妻, not Lady Cai.

proposals.before: The thirteenth year marked Liu Biao's own end and the people's removal toward the north under Cao Cao's Ji Province.
proposals.after: "By the thirteenth year not a sprig is left" means in the thirteenth year Biao too was about to die, and the people were about to move to Ji Province.
proposals.reason: Chinese 民當移詣冀州 does not name Cao Cao.

proposals.before: In Jian'an 3 Yuan Shao crushed him; Zan hanged his kin, set himself ablaze, and Shao's men stormed the tower to take his head.
proposals.after: In Jian'an 3 Yuan Shao attacked Zan; Zan was greatly defeated, strangled his sisters, wife, and children, set fire and burned himself; Shao's troops rushed up the tower and beheaded him.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic collapses 姊妹妻子 into undifferentiated kin and omits the defeat clause.

decisions.reason: 視之如小兒 and 百事自由 mean Chong and the others treated Penzi as a child with a free hand in all affairs, not a puppet confined to trifles; 初不恤錄 is failure to supervise or keep a record, not mere indifference.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 然崇等視之如小兒，百事自由，初不恤錄也。

decisions.reason: 哭不哀 states only that Jing wept without grief; the original invents immediate suspicion and a bier scene, while 作飛書 is composing a flying letter, not a separately inferred secret plot after being suspected.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 山陽王荆哭不哀，作飛書與東海王，勸使作亂

decisions.reason: 故司徒韩寅 is the former Minister of Education (司徒), not a generic former minister; the rest of the proposed sentence keeps the original wording while restoring that office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃拜故司徒韩寅爲司隸校尉

decisions.reason: 后還，遂大亂 names neither an emperor nor exile, and does not say Mo Si was proved right; the original invents subject, exile, and vindication.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 后還，遂大亂。

decisions.reason: 詔以問議郎蔡邕 names Cai Yong as gentleman consultant (議郎), not Master of Writing (尚書); the idiomatic line already has the correct office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 诏以問議郎蔡邕。

decisions.reason: 王莽以后兄子爲大司馬 identifies Wang Mang himself as the empress's elder brother's son who became grand marshal; 'Wang Mang's nephew' inverts the kinship and invents a different appointee.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王莽以后兄子爲大司馬

decisions.after: Xiang Kai argued that the Imperial Academy was where the Qianyi counselors had resided; when its gate gave way of its own accord, it foretold the collapse of moral culture and the abandonment of education.
decisions.reason: 前疑 is the ancient counselor office Qianyi, not a 'doubtful' star; the proposal is right to reject the star reading but wrongly splits 前 as 'former' before a romanized qianyi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 襄楷以爲太学前疑所居

decisions.reason: 六年夏，旱 names the sixth year of the era; 'four years later' is not in the Chinese and, after the neighboring 三年 record, miscounts the interval.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 六年夏，旱。

decisions.reason: 太尉李固勸太后兄梁冀立嗣帝 names Liang Ji as the empress dowager's brother and asks him to establish an heir-emperor; the original drops 太后兄 and flattens 立嗣帝 and 功名不朽.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太尉李固勸太后兄梁冀立嗣帝

decisions.reason: 述遂誅滅 continues Gongsun Shu's given name 述 from 公孙述, not the region 蜀; the literal 'Shu was then executed' reads the person as a place.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 述遂誅滅。

decisions.reason: 迎靈帝 names Emperor Ling only; the personal name Liu Hong is not in this unit and was invented in the idiomatic English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乘舆班班入河間迎靈帝也

decisions.reason: 其母永樂太后 identifies Ling's mother by the Yongle empress-dowager title only; the surname Dong is not in this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其母永樂太后好聚金以爲堂也

decisions.after: Regular palace attendants Guan Ba and Su Kang loathed outstanding worthies of the realm; with the junior privy treasurer of Changle Liu Ao, the chamberlain for ceremonies Xu Yong, and the imperial secretary Liu Fen they formed a clique; Yuan Shansong's Book notes that Liu Fen belonged to the power-broker faction impeached by Fan Pang.
decisions.reason: The original drops 中常侍, 長樂少府, 太常, and 尚書; the proposal restores those offices but over-renders 尚書 as secretariat director (尚書令).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 與長樂少府劉嚣、太常許咏、尚書柳分

decisions.reason: 史侯登蹑至尊 is Marquis Shi's accession; 獻帝未有爵號 is Emperor Xian still without a noble title, and 中常侍段珪 names Duan Gui. The original wrongly seats Liu Xie on the throne.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 史侯登蹑至尊，獻帝未有爵號，爲中常侍段珪等數十人所執

decisions.reason: 中興以來 here is the Han restoration, conventionally the Guangwu restoration; the original does not invent a different event, and the proposed rewrite is only a more literal restyle of an already accurate sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 言自中興以來，荆州无破亂

decisions.reason: 劉表妻當死 names only Liu Biao's wife; Lady Cai is an identification not present in this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 謂劉表妻當死，諸將並零落也

decisions.reason: 民當移詣冀州 says the people were to move to Ji Province; Cao Cao is not named, and 表又當死 is Biao's own coming death.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十三年表又當死，民當移詣冀州也

decisions.reason: 袁紹攻瓚，瓚大敗，縊其姊妹妻子 names an attack, a great defeat, and strangling of sisters, wife, and children; 'hanged his kin' omits the defeat and collapses the kinship list.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 袁紹攻瓚，瓚大敗，縊其姊妹妻子
